intent.primaryUser: A platform operator or architect who wants to see how the platform is wired together.
intent.triggeringNeed: Understanding or demonstrating the breadth of what the platform knows about itself — source code, data model, architecture, and infrastructure — which was only possible through the Neo4j browser before BET-5 retired it.
prerequisites: Signed in with the view_admin capability.
The graph mirror has been populated by the code-graph indexer and the EA/discovery sync.
intent.job: Find a starting point in the corpus and follow its relationships outward to see what it connects to.
intent.successOutcome: The operator can name a thing (a file, a data model, a route, a tool, an EA element), see its neighbourhood drawn, and read its properties and degree.

findability.discoveryCue: A 'Graph Explorer' item in the Advanced family, alongside Platform Development.

deferredRegions.role: Per-label and per-relationship-type facets with live counts.
Raw property map for one node.
deferredRegions.trigger: Operator clicks a node on the canvas.

familyConsistency.terminology: Operator-facing names throughout — 'Source file', 'Data model', 'Route' — never the raw storage labels stored in graph_node.labels.
familyConsistency.actionLocation: Search and depth controls sit above the canvas; per-node actions sit in the right-hand inspector.
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Inline text status (searching, loading, clipped-view notice) — no native dialogs.
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Four choices by default (domain, search, hops, expand); the 12 node labels and 15 relationship types stay behind 'Advanced filters'.
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Reset returns the surface to the census-only state without leaving the route.

empty-corpus.statePredicate: The graph mirror has no rows.
empty-corpus.completionSignal: The census reads zero nodes and zero relationships.
empty-corpus.errorCorrection: The operator runs the code-graph indexer or discovery sync to populate the mirror.

no-starting-point.statePredicate: The corpus is populated but the operator has not chosen a seed node.
no-starting-point.completionSignal: Search results list at least one candidate starting point.
no-starting-point.errorCorrection: An unmatched query explains that nothing matched and suggests a shorter fragment or clearing the domain filter.

neighbourhood-drawn.statePredicate: A seed node is selected and its neighbourhood has loaded.
neighbourhood-drawn.completionSignal: The canvas draws the seed and its neighbours, and the inspector shows the clicked node's labels, properties, and degree.
neighbourhood-drawn.errorCorrection: A clipped view states the node cap and names the three ways to narrow it — relationship filter, node-type filter, or fewer hops.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Find the BacklogItem data model in the graph and tell me how many relationships it has.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The inspector shows the BacklogItem node with the Data model label and a relationship count.
falseSuccessConditions: The operator reads a count from the corpus census tiles instead of the node inspector.
The canvas renders but the inspector is never opened, so no per-node evidence is read.
A clipped view is mistaken for the node's complete neighbourhood.
acceptanceThresholds: The starting point is found within three search attempts.
No raw storage label (for example ArchiMate__DataObject) is shown to the operator.
Rendered subgraphs stay within the node cap so the canvas remains interactive.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: Operator asked for the Neo4j-style visual graph exploration capability to return, under Admin, for exploring and demonstrating the corpus and code graph.
BET-5 mirrored the Neo4j graph into graph_node / graph_edge with the same traversal surface, but shipped no visual explorer over it.

intent.primaryUser: Platform operator responsible for keeping the install current and operable.
intent.triggeringNeed: An update is available, running, complete, blocked, or needs recovery.
prerequisites: The operator is authenticated with platform administration authority.
intent.job: Understand the current update state and take the one safe next action.
intent.successOutcome: The install reaches the intended version and returns healthy, or the operator reaches a truthful governed recovery path.

deferredRegions.role: Version detail, business impact, recovery facts, and concise risks
Technical deploy controls, run history, local-change ledger, and diagnostics

familyConsistency.actionLocation: Co-located with the plain-language release status
familyConsistency.feedbackPrimitive: Report-kit Notice with an announced status
familyConsistency.disclosurePattern: Operational status and next action first; technical evidence in one details disclosure
familyConsistency.returnBehavior: Remain in Platform operations after completion or recovery

update-available.statePredicate: The target lineage is newer than the deployed lineage and no run is active.
update-available.completionSignal: The request is acknowledged and the state advances to queued or running.
update-available.errorCorrection: A failed request is announced beside the action with a recovery route.

queued-or-running.statePredicate: The latest run is queued, pending, running, or completing.
queued-or-running.completionSignal: A terminal run state and healthy served lineage replace progress.
queued-or-running.errorCorrection: A stalled or failed run exposes governed recovery without a duplicate start.

current.statePredicate: Status is available, no run is active or failed, and the deployed lineage is fresh or there is no newer target lineage.
current.completionSignal: The running version and healthy state are visible.
current.errorCorrection: A contradictory target or health signal advances to the matching scenario.

failed-recoverable.statePredicate: The latest governed run failed and the portal remains available.
failed-recoverable.completionSignal: The operator reaches the governed recovery controls and diagnostic evidence.
failed-recoverable.errorCorrection: The failure reason and recovery guidance remain available without hiding the running version.

blocked.statePredicate: Status is unavailable, or a newer target exists and Self-Upgrade is disabled, the job engine is unhealthy, or required scheduling context is missing.
blocked.completionSignal: The operator reaches the owning prerequisite or recovery guidance.
blocked.errorCorrection: The blocker names the missing prerequisite instead of offering a blind retry.

taskProtocol.taskPrompt: Your platform needs attention. Find the update status and safely bring it current, or reach the correct recovery path.
taskProtocol.completionOracle: The served platform lineage matches the intended target and health is green, or the governed recovery surface is reached for a blocked or failed state.
falseSuccessConditions: The update is queued but never reaches a terminal healthy state.
The page reports current while deployed and target lineage disagree.
The operator opens raw logs without reaching the state-appropriate action or recovery.
acceptanceThresholds: The operator finds Self-Upgrade from Delivery > Track & release without search or a supplied URL.
The state-appropriate action or message is fully visible in the first viewport.
Desktop pointer, keyboard, 390 touch, mobile landscape, and 320 CSS-pixel reflow reach the same outcome.

intentEvidenceRefs.summary: The operator requested an efficient, purpose-led Self-Upgrade experience with progressive disclosure.
The Purpose Contract program decomposed the evaluator and Self-Upgrade pilot as an independently shippable slice.
The owner summary already projects update state, impact, reversibility, and next action from canonical status.

consequentialAction.noActionConsequence: When automatic updates are enabled the update waits for the next governed window; otherwise it remains pending.
consequentialAction.reversibility: The governed runner creates a recovery point before the update.
consequentialAction.confirmation: The operator explicitly starts or confirms any force or rollback action.
consequentialAction.authority: Only an authenticated platform operator may execute update or recovery commands.
consequentialAction.recovery: Failure retains the running version or restores the saved recovery point and links to the owning recovery guidance.
